input: Handover on the export job before I go on leave, and I am dictating this in the car so bear with me. The job runs at five past two in the morning off the scheduler, not off cron, and that matters because the scheduler retries and cron does not. It reads yesterday's rows out of the warehouse, writes a CSV, and drops it on the SFTP box for the bank, and the bank picks it up some time before nine. When it fails, and it fails about once a fortnight, it is nearly always the SFTP side rather than our side, and the way you tell is the log. The log is at slasher var log exports slasher nightly dot log and the last hundred lines are enough, you do not need to go digging further back than that. If you see a connection reset in there it is them, and the fix is to rerun with the same date argument, the job is idempotent so a second run does not double the file. If you see a schema error it is us, and that means somebody added a column upstream without telling anybody, which has happened twice this year. Do not change the header order to make it pass, the bank matches on position and not on name, and a reordered header is silently wrong rather than loudly wrong. Anything you cannot work out, mail me, but honestly it will wait until I am back.

input: Post mortem on the save bug, and I want to write it while I still remember the order things happened in. Players were losing about a minute of progress on mobile, not the whole save, just the last minute, and only when the app was backgrounded rather than closed properly. We thought it was the write being cut off halfway, so the first fix was a flush on pause, and that made no difference at all, which should have told us something. What was actually happening is that the autosave timer kept running after the app went to the background on Android, fired once, and wrote a snapshot taken before the last checkpoint, so the newer save was overwritten by an older one. The reason it only showed up on mobile is that desktop pauses the timer with the window, and the reason it looked like a truncation is that a minute is roughly the autosave interval. The fix is to cancel the timer on pause rather than to flush on pause, and to stamp every snapshot with the checkpoint id so a write can refuse to go backwards. That guard is the part I care about, because it turns a silent data loss into a no op, and in the code it reads if snapshot dot checkpoint less than current dot checkpoint, return, which is three lines and will save us the next one of these.

input: Recap of the launch week for the newsletter, and I will tidy the wording later but the numbers are right. We shipped on the Tuesday rather than the Monday because the store review came back late, which turned out to be lucky, since the Monday was the day everybody was talking about the outage and we would have been invisible. Sign ups on day one were about four hundred, day two about nine hundred, and then it flattened out around three hundred a day, which is roughly what we modelled. The traffic that mattered came from two places, one video and one thread, and neither of them was anything we paid for. If people want to follow along the tag we are using is hash tag sunhouse, and the address for press questions is press at sunhouse dot studio, which goes to me and to Nadia rather than to a shared inbox nobody reads. The thing I would do differently is the changelog, we wrote it the night before and it reads like it, and next time I want it drafted a week ahead with only the numbers filled in at the end. Nothing broke, which after last year feels worth saying out loud, and support had eleven tickets all week and nine of them were password resets.

input: This is the wiring note for the van, the Sprinter, and I am doing it in the garage with the panel open in front of me because on Saturday I will not remember why I decided any of it and I will work it out a second time, which is two hours I do not have. So the battery is the 200 amp hour lithium under the driver side bench, and the bench is where everything lives, the battery, the Victron inverter, the Victron MPPT, and the bus bars, and that is deliberate because every run from that bench is short and short runs are the only reason the cable sizing works at all. Twelve volt is unforgiving. Twelve volt is unforgiving in a way that people who have only wired a house do not expect, because the current is ten times what you are used to for the same power, and so a run that would be fine in a kitchen is a fire in a van. From the battery positive I go 35 millimetre squared to the bus bar with a 200 amp Class T fuse within 150 millimetres of the terminal, and that distance is not a suggestion, 150 millimetres, as close as I can physically get it. The inverter is the 1600 watt Victron and it takes its own pair of 35 millimetre squared straight off the bus bar with a 175 amp fuse of its own, because if I hang it off a shared feed the volt drop when the kettle goes on will brown out the fridge, and I have watched that happen in Anders van and he is still convinced the fridge is faulty. The MPPT is the Victron 100 over 30 and the panels are two 175 watt in series, so I am at about 40 volts open circuit on a cold bright morning which is well inside the 100, and 6 millimetre squared from the roof gland down to the controller is more than it will ever need but the run is nearly four metres and I would rather have the copper than the argument. How much does the compressor fridge actually pull on a hot day, that is the number I do not have, because the sticker says 45 watts and the sticker is measured somewhere that is not the back of a van in August. The distribution side is the part I keep changing my mind about. Twelve volt loads go to the fuse block on the bulkhead, lights on a 5 amp, water pump on a 10, fridge on a 15, USB sockets on a 5, and the diesel heater gets its own 20 amp because it draws a spike at glow plug that trips anything meaner. All of that is 2.5 millimetre squared except the fridge and the heater which are 4. Negative goes back to the same bus bar, one bar, one place, and nothing gets chassis grounded except the negative bus itself at a single point on the seat frame where I have ground the paint back to metal, and if I ever find a second chassis ground in this van it is because someone else has been in here. The shunt goes on the negative side between the battery and the bus bar and nothing at all connects to the battery negative except that shunt, because the moment something sneaks a return past it the state of charge reading is a work of fiction. Cables through the bulkhead get a grommet and a strain relief and I am not going to talk myself out of that on Saturday when I am tired and the grommets are in the other box. Two things still open. The first is whether the solar even earns its keep given I am parked under trees half the year, and the second is the alternator charging, because the B2B I have is a 30 amp and the smart alternator on this engine drops its voltage under light load, which is the whole reason a B2B exists, so I think it is fine, but I want to see it on the Victron app across a real drive before I trust it. Write this up as a proper spec sheet for the inspector, with the fuse ratings and the cable sizes in a table, because he will ask for it and I would rather hand him paper than stand there explaining a bench. And do the labels at the same time, both ends of every cable, because I have opened up other people work where nothing was labelled and I said things about those people that I would not want said about me.

input: Right, Marcelo, the calf, and this is the plan going out to him tonight rather than the version I said in the room because in the room I undersold how long this takes. So he tore the soleus on 14 April, not the gastroc, the soleus, and that distinction is the whole reason we are at week six and still not running, because soleus takes the load every single step and it does not care that he feels fine walking. Today he did double leg calf raises at bodyweight for three sets of fifteen with no next day soreness, single leg at 40 kilos on the smith for three sets of eight, and the isometric hold at 90 seconds which is up from 60 last week. That is a real jump and I want him to sit at 90 for a week before he goes chasing 120. Before he runs a step he needs the single leg raise at bodyweight plus 50 kilos for three sets of ten, and because he keeps cheating that movement through his knee I want it filmed from the side so I can see the ankle actually finish, and so the hop test has to be pain free the morning after and not just on the day, because the morning after is the only honest test there is with a soleus. Week seven is walk run, four minutes walk one minute run, eight rounds, heart rate under 140 and if it goes over 140 he walks until it comes back, and Marcelo will hate that because he ran a 3:12 in Boston and being told to walk feels like an insult. Progression is ten percent a week on total running minutes, not on distance, minutes, because he will make the minutes into distance by running faster if I let him. If it flares I want to know within twenty four hours, not at the next appointment, which is 12 May at half four. And one more thing, Marcelo, the shoes, he has been in the same pair since January and he thinks that is loyalty.

input: This is the note for the bench for Saturday and Marta will read it before me so I say the important thing first. The levain goes at ten in the evening, not eleven, ten, because the kitchen is warmer now and last week it was over by the time we came in and the bread had that acetone edge that the regulars notice even when they cannot name it. Eighty five percent hydration on the country loaf. Eighty five, not ninety, I know Marta likes ninety and I know the crumb is prettier at ninety, but we are shaping four hundred of them and at ninety the dough beats us before we beat it. Autolyse one hour, salt after, bulk at twenty four degrees for four hours with three folds in the first two hours and nothing after that, then divide, bench rest thirty minutes, shape, and into the retarder at four degrees overnight. Bake at 250 falling to 230 with steam for the first twelve minutes and then vent it properly, and I mean open it, because the crust we sent out on Tuesday was pale and chewy and that is a vented oven that was not vented. Ora la parte che non riesco a spiegare in inglese, perche mia nonna lo diceva sempre cosi e io lo sento con le mani prima di vederlo con gli occhi. La pasta e pronta quando non tira piu, quando la tocchi e ti risponde piano, come una guancia, non come una gomma. Se tira, aspetta. Se cede troppo, hai perso, e non c'e niente da fare, la butti nel pane di domani. Non guardare l'orologio, guarda la pasta. Marta, quello che ti ho detto sabato scorso vale ancora, la fretta e l'unico ingrediente che non perdona. So that is the part I cannot say in English and I am not going to try. Ciabatta, we are not doing ciabatta on Saturday, I do not care what the board says, we do not have the oven space and the last three Saturdays we have sold nine of them. Focaccia doubles, two trays, and the rosemary goes on after the first press and not before, because before it burns and then people tell me the focaccia tastes of nothing. Flour order, we are down to about four bags of the tipo zero and the delivery is Tuesday, so if Saturday runs long we borrow from the pizza flour and I will fix the numbers after. Marta, if the retarder reads above six when you come in, ring me, do not just bake it and hope.

Autolyse one hour, salt after, bulk at twenty four degrees for four hours with three folds in the first two hours and nothing after that, then divide, bench rest thirty minutes, shape, and into the retarder at four degrees overnight. Se cede troppo, hai perso, e non c'e niente da fare, la butti nel pane di domani. Non guardare l'orologio, guarda la pasta. Marta, quello che ti ho detto sabato scorso vale ancora, la fretta e l'unico ingrediente che non perdona. So that is the part I cannot say in English and I am not going to try. Focaccia doubles, two trays, and the rosemary goes on after the first press and not before, because before it burns and then people tell me the focaccia tastes of nothing. Flour order, we are down to about four bags of the tipo zero and the delivery is Tuesday, so if Saturday runs long we borrow from the pizza flour and I will fix the numbers after. Marta, if the retarder reads above six when you come in, ring me, do not just bake it and hope.

input: Right, Llanrhos, Tuesday night, six until half eight, and I am doing this in the car before I go in because if I go in first it will not get done. Fourteen doors answered out of forty one knocked, which is better than the last round and much better than the wet one in February, and of the fourteen I would say six are ours, three are gone, and five could go either way depending on who speaks to them last. The bins. It is the bins again. Everything on that estate comes back to the bins, and I know we have said for two years that the collection change is a county matter and not a ward matter, and I know that is true, and I also know that saying it true on a doorstep at ten past seven to a woman who has had seagulls through her rubbish twice in a fortnight makes you sound like every other person who has stood there. The bins are the thing. Whatever else goes in the next leaflet the bins have to be on the front of it. Number 22 is the one I want to come back to properly, a man in his sixties, ex council himself, knew exactly how the contract had been let and told me more about it in four minutes than we have got from three emails to the office, and he is not with us and he is not against us, he is just done, and he said he has not voted since 2019 and he said it like a man stating his address. Number 9 was hostile at the door and then kept talking for twenty minutes, which is usually a good sign. The flats above the pharmacy, 1 to 6, nobody in at all and the intercom is broken so we could not have got in anyway, and that is the third round running those six have not been contacted, so either somebody does a Saturday morning there or we stop counting them as canvassed. What came up, and I am going to say all of it because the pattern matters more than any one of them, was the bins, and then the bus that was rerouted in September and now does not go past the surgery, because two separate people brought that up unprompted and one of them is a carer who now walks it, and then the flooding at the bottom of Bryn Road which everybody says is the drains and the county says is the culvert, and then the state of the playing field which is a genuinely small thing that people care about far more than we act like they do, and then the school places, because the catchment change lands next year and nobody has told the parents anything they trust. That is not a list I want tidied into headings. It came out of people mouths in that order and the order tells you something. Llanrhos is not one place either, and I keep having to remind the committee of this. The top of Llanrhos, the newer houses, they want the road resurfaced and they want it said in a certain tone. The bottom end wants the bins and the bus. Same ward, same leaflet, and we have been writing one leaflet for both ends of Llanrhos for four years and wondering why the returns are flat. Is the print run for the next leaflet actually paid for, because Gwen said it was going through the branch account and Dai said it was coming out of the fighting fund, and those cannot both be right and I do not want to find out in March. Two practical things. The board list is out of date, seven of the addresses on it have moved or died, and I have marked them on the sheet but somebody has to actually put that into the system or I will be marking the same seven in June. And we need a second person on Thursdays, because doing a round alone means you either cut the conversations short or you do half the doors, and tonight I did half the doors. I will type the sheet up tomorrow and the deadline for the leaflet copy is 14 March, which is a Friday, so the copy has to be with the printer on the Wednesday, and if it slips a week it lands in the Easter holidays and nobody reads anything in the Easter holidays.

input: Contest notes, Saturday into Sunday, and I am dictating this before I sleep because the log has to go in within five days and I will not remember the problems by Wednesday. Total was 412 contacts, 38 multipliers, and about nine hours in the chair which is less than I planned because the amplifier tripped twice and I lost the whole of the 0200 to 0400 stretch to it. Conditions on twenty metres were flat until about 0700 UTC and then it opened and it opened properly, and between 0700 and 0930 I put 140 in the log which is nearly a third of the entire weekend in two and a half hours. Does the club claim actually cover the assisted category, because I had the cluster open on the second monitor for the last two hours and if that puts me in assisted then my entry is in the wrong box and I would rather know now than after the results. Worked UR5EQF three times. UR5EQF on twenty at 0714, again on fifteen at 0902, and again on forty at 2210, and all three are legitimate because they are separate bands, but the log checker will flag them and somebody on the reflector will accuse me of padding, so I want the times written down while I still have the paper log in front of me. Signal reports, he was 59 on twenty, 57 on fifteen and a genuinely marginal 33 on forty, and that 33 took four repeats. Best run of the contest was on 14.187, fourteen point one eight seven, and I sat there for fifty minutes without moving because every time I tried to shift up for the noise I lost the frequency to a net that appears out of nowhere on that band at that hour. Grid is KN01, and I had two stations query it and one of them insisted I meant KN00, which I did not, KN01, and I spelled it kilo november zero one three separate times to the same operator and he logged it wrong anyway, which will show up as a not in log next month and I will lose the points and there is nothing to be done about it. The amplifier is the real story of the weekend. It tripped at 0146 and again at 0231, both times on forty metres, both times mid transmission, and both times the SWR reading on the meter looked fine before and after, so either the meter is lying or something in the antenna is arcing when it gets damp, and it was damp. I have a suspicion about the balun on the inverted V, because the last time this happened was also a wet night, and dry weekends I have never seen it. Before the next contest I want to swap that balun and I want to run it at full power into the dummy load for twenty minutes first, because doing that diagnosis at two in the morning in the middle of a run is how you end up with neither a diagnosis nor a run. Rate wise the pattern was the usual one, twenty metres carried the day, fifteen was open for maybe ninety minutes around midday and gave me eleven multipliers I would not otherwise have had, and forty was slow and painful all night for 60 contacts, and eighty I did not touch at all because the noise floor from the neighbour solar inverter is now so high that eighty is effectively gone for me until somebody fits a filter, and it will not be the neighbour who fits it. Logging software behaved apart from one thing, it dropped the band change at 0902 and put the fifteen metre contacts in as twenty, and I caught it because of UR5EQF, because I knew I had already worked UR5EQF on twenty and the duplicate warning did not fire when it should have. So the log has fifteen minutes of contacts around 0902 that I have corrected by hand and I want somebody who knows the Cabrillo format to look at the file before I submit it, because if the band fields are wrong the checker will not just drop those, it will start looking at everything. Antenna for next year, either I get the forty metre element up another four metres or I stop entering the night hours and treat this as a daytime single band effort, and honestly the second option is more fun and less money. 412 contacts, 38 multipliers, and the claimed score comes out around 68,000 before any penalties, which is up on last year despite losing two hours, and that is entirely the 0700 opening on twenty.

input: Claim HV-2291-04, the Ferreira property on Bloubergstrand, date of loss the fourteenth after the front came through overnight, and I am on the roof so this will be short and I will do the proper report at the office. HV-2291-04. Damage is real and it is storm damage and I am going to say that first because the insurer has already asked me twice whether this is wear. Six sheets lifted on the north western slope, three of them gone entirely and two of those recovered from the neighbour driveway which I have photographed where they landed, and the fixings that are still in place have pulled through rather than sheared, which is uplift and not fatigue. Battens are sound. Underlay is torn across roughly 2.4 metres running with the slope and there is water staining on the ceiling boards in the back bedroom over an area I would put at 1.8 by 1.2, and the moisture meter reads 24 percent in the worst of it against 11 on the same board three metres away. Now the ridge. The ridge is pre-existing. The ridge is pre-existing and I want that in the file in plain words, because the pointing along the ridge has failed along most of its length and it has failed slowly, there is vegetation growing out of two of the joints, and no storm on the fourteenth or any other night put vegetation in there. So the ridge comes out of the claim and the sheets and the underlay and the ceiling go in, and the insured is not going to like that split and I have told him so on site rather than letting him read it in a letter. Excess is 5,000 and my estimate for the covered work is 34,000 to 41,000 depending on whether the ceiling boards can be dried and painted or have to come down, and I will not know that until the drying company has been in for a week. Get the drone photos into the file before the insurer rings on Monday, because the ground level shots do not show the pull through and the pull through is the entire argument. Contractor quote is due the eighteenth and I have asked for it itemised by slope.

input: Incident log, Cormac Doyle, second year, Thursday afternoon, and I am putting this in tonight rather than tomorrow because last time I left it and the detail went. This started in the corridor and not in my room, and that matters. It started in the corridor. At about ten past two, between periods, there was something between Cormac and another boy that I did not see the beginning of, and by the time I came out of Room 14 Cormac was up against the lockers and the other boy had walked off, and when I asked him what happened he said, and I am quoting him because the wording is the thing that concerns me, he said I am going to absolutely wreck him, he is a little shit and everybody knows it. I have written that as he said it because if this goes to a meeting with his mother I am not going to be the person who tidied it up. Was the thing before half term ever actually logged, because I raised it with the year head and I never saw it come back on the system, and if there is no record of that one then this one reads as a first incident and it is not a first incident. In class afterwards, half two to twenty past three, he was quiet, did no work, refused to open the book, and when I asked him a second time he put his head down on the desk and stayed there, and I left him there because the alternative at that point was a scene in front of twenty six of them and nothing would have been gained. Cormac is not a difficult boy in the ordinary sense. He is a boy who has had a bad six weeks and who is now in the corridor at every break with the same two lads, and the corridor is where all of this keeps starting. I have not put him on report. I want to speak to him on his own on Friday morning before anybody puts him on anything, and I want the year head to tell me whether October is on the record first.

input: Right, apiary walk, second of May, warm enough that they were all flying by half nine, and I am doing this at the truck with the smoker still going so if it cuts off that is why. Hive 1, twelve frames, brood on eight of them, queen seen, marked blue which is last year so she is doing a second season and doing it well, eggs in a proper pattern, no queen cells, and I gave them a second super because the sycamore is about to go and they will fill it in ten days if the weather holds. Hive 2, same story but a frame behind, no queen seen but eggs on four frames so she is in there, and I did not keep looking because there is no reason to keep pulling frames apart once you have found eggs. Hive 3 is the split I made in April and it has taken, the new queen is laying, unmarked because I have not caught her yet, and the pattern is patchy in a way that is normal for a young queen in her first three weeks so I am leaving it alone until the sixteenth. Hive 4 and hive 5 are boring and I mean that as praise. Hive 6 is light, they came through the winter thin and they have not caught up, four frames of brood and a lot of empty comb, and I have moved a frame of sealed brood in from hive 1 to give them bodies, which is the only real intervention I have made all morning. Now hive 7. Hive 7 is the one. Hive 7 has been the one since February and I have been telling myself a story about hive 7 all spring, which is that they are just slow, and I do not think that story survives this morning. There are no eggs. There are no eggs anywhere in hive 7, there is sealed brood that is emerging so there was a queen three weeks ago, and there is one queen cell on the face of the fourth frame that has been opened from the side, which is a bee killing a queen rather than a queen emerging, and that is the bit I keep coming back to. Mite count on hive 7 came out at nine per hundred bees on the alcohol wash, which is over the treatment threshold on its own, and my working theory is that they went into the spring carrying too much varroa, the queen failed, they tried to replace her, and something went wrong with the replacement. Before the main flow comes in I need to make a decision on hive 7, and I want to combine them into hive 6 rather than requeen them because two weak colonies limping is worse than one decent one, and so that means finding out for certain whether there is a virgin in there before I do anything irreversible, and because a newspaper combine over a queenless colony with a hidden virgin ends with a dead queen and a fight, I am going to give them a test frame of eggs from hive 1 on the ninth and come back three days later to see whether they draw cells on it. That is not a checklist, it is one decision with three conditions hanging off it and it needs to read the way I said it. Treatment, and this is the part I will get wrong if I do not write it down, the oxalic dribble is 3.2 percent solution, 5 millilitres per seam of bees, and I am not doing it on any colony with sealed brood because it does not touch mites under the cappings and all it does is stress them, so hive 7 gets treated after the emerging brood is out and not before, which is roughly the twenty third. Hive 8 is the swarm I caught off the church wall last year and they are the strongest thing in the yard, two supers already, and they are the ones I will take honey off first. Equipment, I am three supers short if the sycamore does what it did in 2023, and there is no point ordering frames in June because everybody orders frames in June. Hive 7 again, one last thing, I left the entrance reduced to about an inch because if they are queenless and weak they will get robbed and robbing is how a bad hive becomes an empty one overnight. Notes for the association meeting, the mite counts across the whole yard averaged four per hundred which is fine, but the spread was one to nine and the nine is hive 7, so an average across an apiary tells you nothing useful and I want to say that out loud because half the people there treat on an average.

input: Board three, third round, and I lost a game I was not losing, so I want this down before I look at an engine and let it tell me what I already suspect. He played the Sicilian, Najdorf, and I went into the English Attack with 6. Be3 e5 7. Nb3, which is the line I have played maybe forty times and know better than anything else in my repertoire, ECO B90, and out of the opening I was completely fine, maybe slightly better, with the space on the queenside and his light squared bishop doing nothing on b7 for about fifteen moves. Move 23. Everything is move 23. On move 23 I had the choice between Nd5 and f4, and I played Nd5 almost instantly, maybe forty seconds, with an hour and ten still on my clock, and that is the mistake, not the move itself but playing it in forty seconds because I had seen the same shape in a Kasparov game and my hand moved. Was Nd5 actually losing, or was it just worse, because that changes what I take from this entirely, and I do not want to know from the engine yet, I want to work out what I thought I saw. After 23. Nd5 Bxd5 24. exd5 Nd4 he gets the knight into d4 for free and my b3 knight is gone and suddenly the position is not about my queenside space at all, it is about his knight sitting in the middle of my position with no way to challenge it, because the c pawn is on c2 and cannot go to c3 without dropping the d pawn. f4 was the move. f4, exf4, Bxf4, and the dark squared bishop comes alive and the d5 square is still available later on my terms and not on his, and the reason I did not play it is that I did not like giving up the e5 square, which is the kind of general reason that loses games to concrete ones. Then between move 26 and move 34 I defended reasonably well, I found Qe1 which was the only move twice in a row, and I got to move 34 with a position that was unpleasant but holdable, a rook and knight each with pawns on both sides, and at that point I had eighteen minutes and he had forty. Move 35 I played Kf1 when Kh2 holds, and that is a genuinely losing move, and I played it because I was down to eighteen minutes in a position I had already been suffering in for ten moves, which is the same mistake as move 23 wearing different clothes. I do not have a time management problem in the sense of running out of time. I have a problem where I spend nothing on the critical move and then twenty minutes on the move after it, when the critical move was the one that decided the game. That is the third time this season. His rating is 2105, mine is 2038, and the loss puts me back under 2030 which I do not actually care about, but the way I lost is the same way I lost in November and in January, and both of those were also a fast move at the exact moment the position changed character. So the work is not opening work. My opening prep is fine, I was fine out of the opening, I have been fine out of the opening in every game this season. The work is recognising the moment the position stops being the one in the book, and the honest signal for that is when I catch myself thinking about a game I have seen rather than the board in front of me, because both November and today I could tell you exactly which famous game I was pattern matching against. Practical fix, and this is the only thing from tonight I actually want to remember, when a knight jump into the centre is available and it is not forced, I stop and I use ten minutes, every time, no exceptions, because that is the shape of position where I have now lost three games. Move 23 was forty seconds. I will look at the engine on Thursday and not tonight, because tonight I would just be looking for the line that makes me feel better about Nd5.

input: Condition report, accession 1974.212, oil on canvas, 61.5 by 48.2 centimetres, attributed to the workshop rather than the hand and dated somewhere between 1660 and 1680, examined this morning in the study room under raking light and then under UV, and Bergsma was with me for the second half of it so anything I say about the varnish is her reading and not mine. Overall the painting is stable and I am going to say that at the top because the borrower has been told a version of this by somebody who saw it in 2019 and the 2019 note is more alarming than the object deserves. The support is the original canvas, lined at some point I would guess in the nineteenth century with a glue paste lining that has gone slightly brittle at the edges but is doing its job, and there is cusping visible along the top and left edges which tells you the original tacking margins are still there under the lining, which is good news and worth recording because it is the sort of thing that gets lost between reports. Craquelure is age appropriate, a fine net pattern across the sky, wider and more mechanical in the dark passages of the lower right where the paint is thickest, and there is no active cleavage, nothing lifting, nothing that moved when Bergsma tapped along the lower edge with the back of a fingernail. The tear. There is a tear, it is the thing everybody asks about, it runs about 4.5 centimetres diagonally through the sitter's right shoulder, it was repaired at the time of the lining, and it is stable. The tear is stable. I want that written twice because the 2019 note describes it as vulnerable and Bergsma and I both examined it this morning and there is no deformation, no tenting along the join, and the fill is slightly proud of the surrounding paint which is cosmetically visible in raking light and structurally irrelevant. Under UV the varnish fluoresces unevenly, so there has been at least one partial cleaning, and there is retouching in the background to the left of the head over an area of maybe 6 by 4 centimetres that is not visible in normal light and reads as a dark island under UV, and a second smaller campaign of retouching along the tear itself. The varnish is yellowed but even, and Bergsma is against any intervention before the loan, and I agree with her, because a partial clean before a journey is the worst of both options. What the courier needs to know is that the frame is not original, it is a nineteenth century replacement with a rebate that is slightly too shallow, so the painting sits forward in it and the top edge of the canvas is in contact with the frame lip, and if it travels like that in a crate that gets cold the contact point is where a problem will start, and so a strip of felt at the rebate before it goes anywhere is not optional, and because the glazing they have proposed adds weight to the front, the whole thing needs its hanging hardware checked at their end rather than ours. That is one requirement with three consequences and I do not want it read as three separate items. Environment, and this is the standard language, 50 percent relative humidity plus or minus 5, 20 degrees plus or minus 2, and 150 lux at the surface with a total exposure I would want capped for the run of the exhibition. Put the raking light photographs into the loan file alongside this, all eleven of them including the four of the tear, because the next person to look at this object will be a stranger reading a folder and the photographs are the only thing that will stop them repeating the 2019 sentence. One outstanding question for the registrar, is the crate the borrower has specified the one that came back from The Hague, because if it is then the interior fittings are cut for a smaller frame and somebody will find that out on a loading dock. Recommendation is that the loan proceeds, with the felt at the rebate, with the courier present at both unpacking and repacking, and with a condition check on arrival that specifically records the state of the fill at the shoulder so that we have a before and after on the one feature anybody will argue about.

input: Trench four, end of day, and this is the context sheet for 1042 dictated in the trench because I want it recorded before I climb out and start doubting myself. 1042 is the fill of the ditch cut we assigned 1043 last Thursday, and the relationship is unambiguous, 1042 sits in 1043 and both are cut through the natural at about 0.85 below datum, and 1042 is overlain by 1039 which is the spread of stone we spent two days deciding was not a surface. So the sequence from the top is 1039, then 1042, then the cut 1043, and then natural. 1042 is a mid greyish brown silty clay, moderately compact, with frequent small subangular stone inclusions and occasional charcoal flecks, and the charcoal is not evenly distributed, it concentrates in the lower 0.15 of the fill towards the northern edge, which is why I have taken the bulk sample from there and not from the middle. Sample 24, ten litres, from the base of 1042 at the north. Thickness of 1042 varies, 0.42 at the northern end where we have the full profile and only 0.18 where the modern service trench 1017 has clipped it, and I want that variation on the record because the section drawing will make it look uniform and it is not. Finds from 1042 are not spectacular and that is fine. Small find 112 is a copper alloy pin fragment, no head, recovered from the upper part of the fill, and small find 113 is a fragment of what Dana thinks is a rotary quern and I think is a piece of structural stone that has been dressed on one face, and we have agreed to disagree in writing until somebody who knows stone looks at it. Pottery from 1042 is eleven sherds, all of them abraded, and the two rim sherds are the only ones anybody will be able to say anything about. Before this trench is backfilled on Friday I need the section drawn at 1 to 20 with 1042 and 1043 both fully annotated, and because the light at the northern end is impossible after two I want the photographs done in the morning with the scale and the north arrow actually in frame this time, and so the levels need reshooting off the temporary benchmark rather than off the peg we have been using, since I do not trust that peg after somebody drove the dumper past it. That is one requirement with three conditions and it needs to read as I said it, not as three bullet points on a sheet somebody skims. Interpretation, and I am putting this in as interpretation and clearly labelled, 1043 is not a boundary ditch. It is too shallow, the profile is too irregular, and it does not continue into trench five where it should if it were running on the alignment the geophysics suggested. What I think 1043 is, is a quarry scoop or a series of them, dug to get at the gravel, and 1042 is what people threw in afterwards over a fairly short period, which would explain the charcoal concentration and the abraded pottery and the general look of the thing. Were the environmental samples from last season ever actually floated, because if they were and there is nothing in them then my short period argument is weaker than I am about to write it up as, and I have asked twice and nobody seems to know who has the residues. Grid reference for the trench corner is SE 4471 2938 and the datum is the one on the fence post, 42.31 metres, and I say that every day into these notes because the second datum somebody established behind the spoil heap is 0.6 out and two people have used it. 1042 again, one last thing, there is a patch at the very base against the northern edge of the cut that may be a separate deposit rather than part of 1042, it is greyer and it is stonier, and I have not given it a number because I could not convince myself in the light we had, so tomorrow morning that gets looked at first and if it is a separate deposit it becomes 1044 and half of what I have just said about the charcoal belongs to 1044 and not to 1042.

input: Dive one on the Hokuriku, and I am doing this on the boat with wet hands so it will be blunt. Maximum depth 38.4 metres. 38.4, which is deeper than the plan, the plan was 36, and the reason we went to 38.4 is that the swim through at the stern drops away and neither of us noticed until the computer started complaining. Bottom time 24 minutes, gas was 32 percent nitrox, and 32 percent at 38.4 puts me at about 1.4 partial pressure which is at my limit and not over it, but there is no margin left in that number and I do not want to repeat it. Did the deco obligation actually clear before we surfaced, because my computer showed three minutes at six metres and Trung computer showed five at six and three at nine, and we did the longer of the two, but the two devices disagreeing by that much on the same profile is the thing I want to look at tonight. Surface interval is 58 minutes so far and I am not getting back in until it is over ninety. Visibility was maybe eight metres at the top of the wreck and closer to three at the sand, which is worse than the last two times I have been on the Hokuriku, and there is silt through the whole midships section now that was not there in March. The stern gun is still there and still swings, the hold is open and I went in about four metres and came out because Trung was not behind me, and I would rather lose a penetration than lose a buddy. Air, I came up with 60 bar which is tighter than I like, and it is tight because of the extra two metres and because I spent five minutes trying to free a line somebody has left tied to the railing. Somebody has left a line on the Hokuriku railing, orange, about eight millimetres, and it is going to kill somebody in low visibility. Thermocline at 22 metres and it was 18 degrees below it, and the 5 millimetre was not enough for 24 minutes, so tomorrow I am in the 7 or I am not doing the second deep one. Trung ears were slow on the descent, we stopped twice, and that is worth writing down because it is the second dive in a row.

input: Right, plot 31, second Saturday in September, and the courgettes have beaten me again. The courgettes have beaten me. I planted four and everybody told me to plant two and I planted four because I am an idiot with a seed tray in March, and I have now given courgettes to every single person I work with and two of them have started avoiding me. Bed three is the good news. Bed three has been the best bed on the plot all year, the leeks in there are thicker than the ones in bed one and they went in the same week from the same tray, and the only difference is the manure I put on bed three in February and did not put anywhere else, which is either a lesson or a coincidence and I am going to treat it as a lesson. The Cobra beans are done, I have pulled the poles down and left the roots in because somebody on the site told me that is the whole point of beans and I have decided to believe him. Tomatoes were a disaster, blight came through in the third week of August and took the lot in about nine days, and I got maybe two kilos off six plants before it did. Soil test came back at 6.4 which is fine, slightly acid, nothing I need to do about it this year. Going in next is the garlic, and then the broad beans in November if the ground is not sodden, and then I want to get the green manure on bed two and bed four before the end of the month because bare soil over winter is how bed four ended up like concrete last spring. Bed three gets nothing over winter except a mulch, because I am not touching whatever is working in bed three. Order the garlic this week, the Solent Wight, not the supermarket stuff, because last year I forgot until October and planted it in December and got bulbs the size of a two pence piece. Shed roof is leaking again at the back corner. And the rhubarb needs moving but I have said that for two years so let us not pretend.

input: Right, so the Whitby trip, and I am doing this now because Kev wants the write up for the club page by Friday and if I leave it I will forget the marks. We went out of the harbour at 5:40 on the Saturday, three of us, me and Kev and Kev's brother in law whose name I still cannot say properly, and the forecast was two to three from the north east which was fine on paper. The tide was wrong. I am going to say that again because it is the whole story of the day, the tide was wrong, we were fishing the back end of the ebb on the Rosa mark when we should have been sat on it for the flood, and Kev knew it, I knew it, and we went anyway because the skipper had the slot booked. First drift we had nothing at all, and then over the same ground we had four codling between us, none of them anywhere near size, and after that the wind came round to the east and knocked the drift out completely so we were dragging over the rough and losing gear. I lost two sets of pirks in about twenty minutes, which at £9 a set is money I would rather have spent on diesel. We moved inshore to the 30 metre ground off Sandsend at about half eleven and that is where the day turned, because on the slack we had thornbacks one after another, seven in the boat and two off at the side, biggest one Kev had at about 8 lb which he weighed twice because nobody believed him. Kev weighed it twice. Anyway, the honest summary for the club page is that the fish were there and the plan was shit, and if we book that slot again we book it for two hours later, and I will say that to the skipper myself rather than letting Kev do it.

input: This is my note from the governors meeting on Tuesday, the full body not the resources committee, and I am dictating it on the way home because the clerk only takes decisions and half of what mattered was not a decision. We had eleven of us in the room and Priya chaired because Alan is still off, and the head's report ran to twenty minutes which is longer than usual because of the attendance figures. Attendance is at 91.4% against a target of 95.5%, and the persistent absence figure is the one that worried people, 19 pupils above the ten per cent threshold in the autumn term against 11 in the same term last year. input: I am putting the whole rent thing in order before I send anything to the tribunal, so this is the timeline and nothing else, no opinions, just what happened and when. The tenancy started on 1 September 2024 at £985 a month, joint tenancy, me and Sadaf, deposit £1,138 which is protected with the Deposit Protection Service under reference DPS-4471-9930. The rent goes out on the twenty ninth of every month by standing order from the joint account, and I want to be very clear about this because it is the thing they keep getting wrong, I paid on the twenty ninth. Every month, on the twenty ninth. The bank statement shows it and I have the statements from September 2024 through to February 2026 saved as PDFs. In November 2025 the agent, that is Hartwell Residential, not the landlord directly, sent a notice saying the rent would go to £1,120 from 1 January 2026, which is a 13.7% increase, and the notice came by email on 22 November with no section 13 form attached. I replied on 24 November asking for the form and got nothing. I chased on 3 December and on 11 December, both by email to lettings@hartwellresidential.co.uk, and the only response was an automated one. Then on 2 January the standing order went out at the old amount because I never changed it, and on 6 January they emailed to say the account was in arrears of £135 and that a fee of £25 had been added. On 9 January I called and spoke to someone called Dean who said the increase was valid because it was in the email, and I said it was not on the correct form, and he said he would get back to me. On 20 January the arrears letter came by post, dated 16 January, showing £295 outstanding, which is two months of the difference plus the fee plus a second fee I have never had explained. I paid on the twenty ninth of January as usual, at £985, and I have not paid anything they call a fee. That is the position as of today. The two documents I still need are the section 13 form, if one exists, and the itemised breakdown of the £295, and I have asked for both in writing on 22 January and again on 4 February.

input: Ok, this is the inventory for the move, and I am walking round the house saying it out loud because the removal firm wants a list and my handwriting is a disaster. Front room first. Two bookcases, the tall pine one and the low one, and the low one has a wobble on the back left leg so it needs to travel flat. Sofa, three seater, and it came in through the window in this house so it is going out through the window in this house, which I have told them twice and I will tell them again on the day. Out through the window. Television, 55 inch, no original box, so that is one of the ones I want blanketed and strapped and not stacked. Then there are eleven boxes already taped in the front room and all of them are marked kitchen, which sounds wrong, and it is wrong, but I packed the kitchen first and I ran out of floor in there, so the box marked kitchen in the front room is a kitchen box, the box marked kitchen in the hall is a kitchen box, and the box marked kitchen in the front bedroom is also a kitchen box. Nothing marked kitchen is in the kitchen. Kitchen itself, the white goods stay, that is in the contract, the fridge freezer and the dishwasher stay with the house, but the small chest freezer in the utility comes with us and it needs defrosting the night before or we will have water in the van. Six boxes of crockery in the utility, wrapped in newspaper not bubble wrap because I ran out, and one of them has a red cross on the lid which means my mother's willow pattern is in there and if anything on this whole list gets broken I would rather it was the television. Upstairs. Front bedroom, bed frame comes apart, the allen key is taped to the headboard, mattress is a king and it will not go round the turn at the top of the stairs so it goes out over the bannister, and I know that because it came in over the bannister. Wardrobe is flat pack and it is coming apart because it has been apart twice already, so honestly if it does not survive I am not going to cry about it. Back bedroom, two single beds, one chest of drawers with the drawers still full because they are just clothes and the drawers do not fall out, and a desk that is going to the tip rather than the new house, so please leave the desk. Leave the desk. Bathroom is nothing, one box. Loft is the problem, there are somewhere between twelve and twenty boxes in the loft and I genuinely do not know which because I have not been up since October, and they are not marked at all, so budget an hour for the loft on its own. Garage, garden tools, two bikes, a workbench that is bolted to the wall and is staying, the lawnmower which is coming, and about forty tins of paint that I will take to the household waste place myself before the day. That is the lot, except the plants along the side path, which are coming, and I will move those in the car myself because the last firm killed a fig tree.

input: This is the overnight schedule for the new bakery shift and I want it in my own words before I write the card that goes on the wall, because the way it is written now nobody can follow it. So we work back from the counter. Bread on the shelf at 7 o'clock, which means out of the oven from 5:30, which means the first tray goes in at 5:00, which means the dough has to be shaped by 4:15 and it has to have come out of the fridge by 3:45 so it has an hour to lose the cold. That is the whole chain and everything else hangs off it. The starter gets fed twice, once at 2 in the afternoon and once at 9 in the evening, both at 1 to 5 to 5 by weight, so 40 grams of starter, 200 of water at 30 degrees, 200 of flour, and the second feed is the one that matters because that is the one we build on. Mix is at 10 in the evening. Eighteen kilos of flour, 78% hydration, 2% salt, and 20% of the total flour weight as leaven, and the salt goes in after the first rest not with the water, and I know some people do it the other way and I do not care, in this kitchen the salt goes in after the rest. Then bulk from half ten to about half two depending on the room, and this is the part nobody can write down properly, because it is not a time, it is a look. Guarda l'impasto, non l'orologio. That is what my grandmother said to me and that is what is going on the card, in Italian, exactly like that, and then underneath it in English it can say watch the dough and not the clock, but the Italian goes first. Divide at half two, sixteen pieces at 900 grams for the big loaves and the rest into 450 gram pieces for the tins, preshape, twenty minutes on the bench, final shape, into the bannetons, and into the retarder at 3 degrees. Now, the thing that went wrong last week. The retarder was at 6 degrees, not 3, because the door had been left on the latch, and the whole batch overproofed and we sold flat bread and called it ciabatta, which was funny for one day and would not be funny twice. So the last thing on the card, and I want this in capitals or in red or however you do it, is check the retarder temperature before you leave and write the number down. Write the number down. If the number is not written down then nobody checked. Focaccia is separate and it does not go in this schedule at all, that one is a morning job and Nadia does it her own way and it works, so I am not touching it.

input: Firing log for the reduction glaze firing, kiln two, and I am dictating this at the kiln because if I write it up tomorrow I will smooth it over and I want the actual numbers. Loaded Thursday afternoon, three shelves, and the pack is not even, top shelf is mostly the small test tiles and the two porcelain bowls, middle shelf is the six stoneware jars for the Kadikoy order, bottom shelf is the big platter on its own with the props at the corners because that platter has warped for me twice and I am not letting it warp a third time. Cones in the spy hole at cone 9 and cone 10, and a cone 8 as a warning, all three visible from the lower spy which is the only one I trust because the upper one has a chip in the glass and everything looks paler through it. Candled overnight from 9 in the evening at about 90 degrees, burners on the lowest setting either side, damper wide open, and by 6 in the morning the pyrometer read 148 which is roughly what it always reads after a candle so nothing surprising. Then the climb. Half past six I brought it up to a hundred degrees an hour and held that shape until about 600, and between 200 and 400 I slowed it down because the platter is thick at the foot and I have cracked a platter on the way up before, so that section took nearly two hours and it was worth it. From 600 to 950 I let it run, closer to a hundred and forty an hour, no drama, atmosphere still oxidising, damper at about a third. At 1004 I started reduction, and this is the number I always get wrong when I write it from memory so I am saying it now, 1004, not 1000 and not 1010, because the reduction on this kiln takes about four minutes to establish and if I start it at 1010 I am into body reduction before the glaze has begun to seal. Twenty minutes of heavy reduction, back pressure at the lower spy showing a flame of about 30 centimetres, and the room filled up because the extractor is not good enough and I have said that to the studio committee three times now. I have said it three times. Then neutral through to 1180, which took another hour and fifty, and the pyrometer and the cones disagreed at the end by what looked like half a cone, cone 9 fully down and cone 10 at four o'clock, so I called it and held for twenty minutes with a light reduction and shut down at 1192 on the pyrometer at ten past four in the afternoon. Total firing time from candle to shutdown, nineteen hours and ten minutes, and gas consumption I will get from the meter tomorrow because the meter is behind the pallets and I am not moving pallets tonight. Cooling with the damper closed and both spies bunged, and I will crack it at 200 which is Saturday morning at the earliest. Now the other thing, and this is for me not for the log. Ozan asked me to write this up as a proper firing report for the studio noticeboard and to make it sound professional and to put the temperatures in a table, and I am not doing that from this dictation, this is my rough log and it stays rough, so whoever reads it can take the numbers out themselves. The results, when I get them, are the only part that goes on the noticeboard anyway. One last note before I lose it, the small test tiles on the top shelf were the new ash glaze at 4% iron and 8% iron and I want to see those before anything else because if the 8% has gone black again then that recipe is finished and I will stop trying to save it.

input: Night shift log for Wednesday into Thursday, gate two, and I am recording this rather than writing it because the pen in the hut has gone again and because there is more to say than fits in the book. Came on at 21:45, took the keys off Yohannes, thirty two keys on the ring and I counted them in front of him because that is the rule now after the November business, thirty two on and I will count thirty two off. Thirty two. The board said four vehicles expected overnight and we had six. First one was the regular, Bekele's truck, plate 3-45872, in at 22:20 for bay four, paperwork correct, out at 23:05, no issue at all. Second was a refrigerated unit that was not on the board, driver had a delivery note for a company called Sahle Trading which is not one of ours, and I would not let him past the barrier, and he sat there for forty minutes on the phone before he accepted that and reversed out. I logged that at 22:50 to 23:30 and I want it noted properly because he will be back and somebody will let him in. He will be back. Third and fourth came together at 01:15 which is exactly what the yard cannot handle, both for bay one, and the second one had to wait outside on the road for twenty five minutes because there is nowhere for a second trailer to stand while the first one is on the dock, and that is the same problem I raised on 3 October and again on 19 October and I have raised it twice and nothing has changed. Fifth was the container at 03:40, seal number CX-9917-44, and the seal was intact, I checked it under the torch and photographed it because the photo is the only thing anybody believes. Sixth was at 05:10, plate 3-71104, and that one is the one to read. The driver came to the window and asked me straight out whether the cameras on the east fence are actually recording or whether they are just sitting there, and I told him that was not a question I answer, and he laughed and said fair enough and went in. I am putting his question in the log word for word because it is the second time this month someone has asked me about the east fence and I do not think that is an accident. Patrols. Four full circuits, 22:00, midnight, 02:30 and 04:45, each one takes about eighteen minutes doing it properly. On the midnight circuit the light over the fuel store was out again, the one on the corner by the bund, and it has been out since the eleventh, and I have written it in the book every night since the eleventh, so that is nine nights. On the 02:30 circuit I found the pedestrian gate on the north side unlocked, not open, unlocked, and I locked it and I do not know who left it, but the last people through there are the cleaners who finish at 20:00 and that is before my shift. On the 04:45 circuit there was a dog inside the fence line near the scrap bay, no collar, and it went out the way it came in which tells me there is a gap under the fence at that corner and somebody should walk it in daylight. Everything else was quiet. Power stayed on, no alarms on the panel, the intruder panel showed one fault at 00:04 which cleared itself in under a minute and that has happened before and the engineer said it was the door contact on the office. I tested the radio twice against the main gate and both times it was fine, which is worth writing down because last week it was not fine. Handed over at 06:05 to Meseret, walked the keys with her, thirty two off the ring and she signed. Thirty two off. The three things for the day shift, and I am not going to pretend any of them are new, are the fuel store light, the gap under the fence at the scrap bay corner, and the fact that two trailers cannot both wait for bay one. And I will say the thing about the east fence question to the supervisor directly rather than leaving it in a book nobody reads.

input: This is where I have got to on the Kelleher side and I am saying it out loud because I have three notebooks going and none of them agree with each other. Start with what is certain. Michael Kelleher, my great grandfather, died in Chicago on 4 February 1931, and the death certificate gives his age as sixty seven, which puts his birth in 1863 or 1864 depending on the month, and the certificate says the birthplace is County Cork with no parish, which is the whole problem in one line. County Cork with no parish. That phrase is on every document I have. The 1900 census has him in Ward 6 with a wife Bridget and four children, and it says immigration year 1884 and naturalised, and the 1910 census has the same household and says immigration 1882, and the 1920 census says 1885, and I want to be careful here because I spent two years trying to make those three agree and they do not agree because the person answering the door told the enumerator whatever they remembered. So the immigration year is a range, 1882 to 1885, and I am going to stop treating it as a fact. Now the part I think is new. input: This is the home programme for Mrs Adeyemi and I am dictating it so the front desk can print it before she leaves, and I want the wording kept plain because last time she told me the sheet read like a car manual. So, right knee, twelve weeks post op, and she is doing better than the notes suggest. Range today was zero to 118 degrees passive and about 112 active, which is up from 104 two weeks ago, and the extension is full and has been full since week six, and that is the thing I want her to know because she keeps apologising for the bend and the extension is the one that matters for walking. The swelling at the end of the day is normal at twelve weeks. It is normal at twelve weeks. She has asked me about it three visits in a row and I want it written on the sheet in those words so she can read it at home when her knee is fat and she is worrying. Exercises stay mostly as they were. Heel slides, twenty a side, twice a day, and she is to go to the point where it is tight and not to the point where it is sharp, and she knows the difference now. Sit to stand from the dining chair, ten reps, three times a day, no hands if she can, one hand if she cannot, and the kitchen counter is not a substitute because the counter is too high and she cheats on it, and I have watched her cheat on it. Step ups on the bottom stair, eight leading with the right, and this is the new one, so she should expect it to feel worse before it feels better and that is not damage. The bike, if she is going to the leisure centre with her daughter on Saturdays, ten minutes at a resistance she can hold a conversation at, and if she cannot hold a conversation the resistance is too high. Walking is where I want the progress. She is doing about fifteen minutes to the shop and back and I want that at twenty five minutes by the next appointment, in one go, not two walks of twelve, because the whole point is the knee under load for a stretch. Now the things to stop. Stop the wall sits, they are doing nothing for her and she hates them, and stop the ice after every single exercise because it is making her think of the knee as an injury and it is not an injury any more, it is a knee that is getting stronger. Ice if it is genuinely sore, not as a ritual. Next appointment four weeks, and if she is at twenty five minutes and 120 degrees I am happy to discharge her with a maintenance sheet. One more thing for the notes and not for her sheet, she mentioned that her husband is in and out of hospital at the moment and she is doing all the driving, and that will be why she has missed two sessions, so if she cancels again do not chase her with the standard letter, just ring her.

input: Right, pressing day, and this is the note for the group chat before I forget who is doing what, and also a bit of a moan, so skip the moan if you want. Saturday, the eighteenth, at Dave's because his barn has the drain and mine does not. Start at nine, and I mean nine, not the usual quarter past ten with three people still in the car park, because the press is booked back to the community orchard on the Monday and if we do not finish we do not finish. Apples. We have got roughly a tonne, which sounds like a lot and is about forty crates, and it is a mess of varieties because everybody brought what fell, so there is a lot of Bramley in there which is going to make it sharper than last year and I am not sorry about that. Last year was flabby. It was flabby and everybody was too polite to say so. If anybody has late Dabinett they should bring it because that is the one thing we are short of and it is the thing that makes it taste like cider rather than juice. Kit. Dave has the press and the scratter and the barrels, I have the hydrometer and the sterilising stuff and about eight demijohns, Priti has the pump and the hoses and the good funnel, and if somebody could bring a second scratter that would change the whole day because the bottleneck is never the pressing, it is the milling, it is always the milling. Jobs on the day. Somebody on the hose washing apples in the trug, two people milling, two on the press, one person doing nothing but moving juice and writing down what went in which barrel, and that last job is the one nobody wants and it is the only one that actually matters in March when we are arguing about which barrel is which. I did it last year. I am not doing it this year, so somebody volunteer or I will pick. Also, bring your own gloves, bring boots, bring a chair for the afternoon, and bring food, because last year we pressed for six hours on two packets of biscuits and Dave's wife had to feed nine adults at four o'clock. Numbers, roughly. A tonne of apples should give us somewhere between 600 and 700 litres if the press behaves, and we are splitting it by weight brought, which we agreed and which I am writing down again because we agreed it last year too and then argued about it anyway. Yeast, we are going wild on the big barrel and pitching on the two small ones, so there is a comparison at the end, and if the wild one goes vinegary again then that settles it for good. Last thing, and this is the actual moan. Three people said last year that they would come and did not, and the same three people were first in the queue for bottles in April, and I am not naming them here but I am naming them in person, and this year the rule is you press or you buy. That is it. Nine o'clock, the eighteenth, Dave's barn, bring gloves.

input: Ok, this is everything about the licence appeal in one place because the hearing is on 12 March and I keep telling it out of order. Licence number PHV-88214, issued 6 June 2023, three year licence, so it runs to June 2026. The complaint that started it was made on 8 January, and the complaint says that on the evening of 4 January I refused a fare and was rude to the passenger, and the passenger's name is not given to me, only a reference, C-2026-0417. On 4 January I worked from 16:00 to 01:30 and I have the app record for every job, twenty three jobs, and the only refusal in the whole shift was at 23:40 at the rank outside the Sathorn office, and it was a refusal because there were four adults and a child and the car is licensed for four passengers. Four passengers. That is on the plate, it is on the licence, and it is the reason, and I said it politely twice and then I said it a third time less politely because the man had his hand on the door. The council wrote to me on 19 January giving fourteen days, and I replied on 27 January with the app record attached and I did not hear anything until 14 February when the suspension notice came, effective immediately, and that is twenty six days of no work as of today. What I need for the hearing is the app record printed with the timestamps rather than emailed, the photograph of the licence plate showing the four passenger limit, and a statement from the office security guard at Sathorn because he was standing there and he saw the whole thing, and his name is Somchai and he works Tuesday to Saturday nights. I have asked the office for his full name twice and they will not give it to me over the phone, so I will go there on Tuesday and ask him myself. Twenty six days. I want that number said at the hearing.

input: This is the rebuild note for the home server, and I am dictating it because I have rebuilt this box twice from memory and both times I forgot the same two things, so this time it is written down. The box is the old Dell tower, 32 GB of RAM, and the disks are four 8 TB drives in a raidz1 plus one 500 GB SATA SSD for the boot pool and one 1 TB NVMe that is doing nothing useful and is going to become the cache. Operating system is Debian 12, minimal install, no desktop, and the first thing after the install is the ZFS packages from backports because the version in stable is older than the pool. The pool is called tank, it was created with ashift=12, and the datasets are tank/media, tank/photos, tank/backups and tank/scratch, and the only one with compression off is tank/media because it is all already compressed video and turning it on just burns CPU for nothing. Mount points go under /srv rather than /mnt, so /srv/media, /srv/photos, and so on, and I chose that two years ago and I am not changing it now because everything in the compose files points there. The compose stack lives in /opt/stack and it is one docker-compose.yml with six services, and the env file is /opt/stack/.env which is the file I forgot last time, and it is the file I forget every time, because it is not in the git repo and it cannot be in the git repo, so it lives in the password manager as an attachment and that is the only copy. The env file is not in the repo. Write that on the front of the note. Services are jellyfin on 8096, paperless on 8000, a postgres 16 container for paperless with its data on tank/backups not on the SSD, syncthing on 8384, caddy doing TLS on 443 with a wildcard certificate from the DNS challenge, and a small uptime checker that I wrote myself and that nobody else needs to understand. Caddy's config is /etc/caddy/Caddyfile and the wildcard is for *.home.reis.dev, and the DNS credentials for the challenge are also in that env file, which is the second reason losing it is a bad afternoon. Snapshots. zfs-auto-snapshot is doing hourly keep 24, daily keep 14, weekly keep 8, monthly keep 6, and that is the same policy I have had since the beginning and it has saved me exactly once, in April, when I deleted a photos directory with a badly written find command and had it back in about ninety seconds. Offsite is restic to Backblaze B2, bucket name reis-home-offsite, running at 03:15 from a systemd timer rather than cron because the timer gives me the failure mail without me doing anything, and the repository password is, again, in the password manager. The exclude file is /opt/stack/restic-excludes and the important line in it is /srv/media because paying to store 6 TB of films I could download again is not a decision anyone should make. Now the two things I forget, and the whole reason this note exists. One, the env file, which I have already said twice and will say a third time at the end. Two, the SMART monitoring, because smartd is not installed by the minimal install and I have twice run this array for months with no disk monitoring at all, which is the single stupidest way to lose a raidz1, so smartmontools goes on before docker does. Order matters there and I always do it backwards. Order of the rebuild, then, and I am saying this as prose because the last time I made it a numbered list I followed the numbers and the numbers were wrong. Install Debian minimal and set the hostname to vault, and then get the backports ZFS in and import the pool read only first to check it before mounting it properly, and then install smartmontools and set the mail address in /etc/smartd.conf before you get distracted, and then docker and the compose plugin from the official repo not from Debian, and then clone the stack repo, and then pull the env file out of the password manager, and only then bring the stack up one service at a time starting with postgres so that paperless does not create its own empty database and confuse itself. Last thing. If I am doing this rebuild in a hurry, which is when it always happens, the temptation is to bring the whole stack up at once and fix what breaks. Do not. Bring postgres up, watch the log, then paperless, then the rest. And the env file is not in the repo.

input: Tank log, and this one is the crash so I want it recorded properly while I still remember the order things happened in, because when I read the forum threads afterwards everybody's account is tidy and mine is not going to be. Setup for the record, 120 litre mixed reef, running since March 2024, so twenty three months, aquascape is two islands, return pump is a DC pump at about 40% of maximum, two gyres on alternating mode, and the lights are a single fixture running a ten hour day with a two hour ramp at each end. Parameters where they normally sit, alkalinity 8.4, calcium 420, magnesium 1350, nitrate 5 to 8, phosphate 0.06, salinity 1.026, temperature 25.5 and it does not move more than 0.3 in a day. Those are the normal numbers and I test alkalinity twice a week with the same kit and the same person doing it, which matters more than which kit it is. What happened. On the Tuesday I did a 20 litre water change, which is a sixth of the volume and slightly more than usual, and I mixed the new water the night before as always and I checked the salinity of the mixed water, 1.026, no issue. On the Wednesday morning two of the acropora had lost colour at the tips, not tissue, just colour, and I did nothing because colour comes back. On the Wednesday evening the same two were pale halfway down and a third one had started, and I tested and alkalinity was 7.6, which is 0.8 down, and that is a bigger single drop than I have ever recorded in this tank. Alkalinity was 7.6. I retested with the same kit and got 7.6 again, and then I made the mistake, and I want it in the log because the mistake is the useful part. I dosed to bring alkalinity back to 8.4 in one go. In one go, in the evening, into a tank that had been dropping all day, and by Thursday morning the three pale corals were bleached at the top third and two more were pale, and the alkalinity read 8.9, so I had overshot as well. What I should have done, and what everybody says and what I know perfectly well, is raise it slowly over three or four days and accept the low number in the meantime, because the corals do not mind 7.6, they mind going from 7.6 to 8.9 in twelve hours. They do not mind the number. They mind the change. Thursday I did nothing except turn the lights down to 60% and stop all dosing, and Friday I tested everything and the only other thing out was nitrate at under 2, which is lower than it should be and is probably why the colour went in the first place, because a 20 litre change on a tank that was already lean will pull nitrate down and pale tips after a big water change on a lean tank is the oldest story in this hobby and I walked straight into it. So the actual cause was not the alkalinity at all, the alkalinity drop was consumption on top of a change, and my response to it is what did the damage. Where it stands now, eleven days later. The three worst are dead at the tips and holding tissue on the lower two thirds, and one of them has started to encrust again at the base which I am taking as a good sign. The two that went pale later have coloured back up completely. Nitrate is at 6 because I have been feeding heavier and stopped running the reactor, phosphate is 0.08, alkalinity has been at 8.2 to 8.4 for a week without me touching it, which tells me the demand dropped because there is less coral to feed. Lights are back to 80% and I will leave them there for another fortnight. Rules for myself, and this is the part I will actually read again. Never correct alkalinity by more than 0.2 in a day, no matter what the number says. Test before a water change as well as after, because I only test after and that is why I did not see the tank was lean. And keep the water change at 15 litres, which is what it was for two years, and stop being clever about it. One more note for whoever reads this if I ever post it, the kit I use reads consistently about 0.2 high against the reference solution, so my 8.4 is somebody else's 8.2, and comparing my numbers to a forum thread without that offset is meaningless.
